basis.text: The licence looked up is ABC Type 47 (on-sale general, eating place), as stated in the description.
The licence is to be obtained by transfer from other premises (a premises-to-premises transfer), as the applicant states.

A Type 47 licence is an on-sale general licence. State law limits these to one for each 2,000 inhabitants of the county; in a county over that number ABC issues no additional one, so the licence comes by transfer of an existing licence unless state law allows otherwise.

North Beach Special Use District: A Restaurant may sell beer, wine or liquor for drinking on the premises (ABC licence Types 02, 23, 41, 47, 49, 59 or 75) only by Conditional Use on the First Story, with a Planning Commission finding that it is and will remain a Bona Fide Eating Place. North Beach Special Use District: To show it is still a Bona Fide Eating Place, the Restaurant had to give the Department, on request, records showing that at least 51% of its gross receipts in the preceding year came from food prepared and sold to guests on the premises. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A), in force since before 2022-01-01).
Census tract 106.00: 52 active on-sale retail licences in ABC's licences as they stood on 9 March 2022, against 12 authorised in ABC's census tract authorisations of September 2026.

The tract is over its authorised number, and state law tests a transfer from other premises for undue concentration. The licence may still issue if public convenience or necessity would be served: public convenience or necessity finding likely required.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 41 approved in 2021 for 411 Columbus (53 m away, same block, North Beach NCD). Planning approved as continuation of existing restaurant use with no expansion, demonstrating recent agency practice on the Columbus corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Most recent comparable (decided October 2021, five months ago) shows Planning routinely approves alcohol licenses for existing restaurants on this block as continuations under §722 and §780.3, provided they operate as bona fide eating places.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 47 referral approved in 2017 for 431 Columbus (same block, 53 m away), also in North Beach NCD. Agency referral confirming Type 47 is permitted as continuation of existing use at a bona fide eating place.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning approved Type 47 continuation at a restaurant literally across the street, citing P.C. §722 and §780.3 and a prior CUA (Motion 16916). Referrals consistently treat established restaurants with Type 47 as continuations requiring no new hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 41 approved in 2021 for 362 Columbus (82 m away, North Beach NCD). Operator converted from Limited Restaurant to Restaurant under Ordinance 182-20 and added Type 41 without CUA or public notice—evidence of recent liberalization for existing food businesses.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning treated the upgrade of an existing eating place to add alcohol as a continuation without requiring a discretionary hearing, showing recent policy favoring established bona fide eating places in North Beach that want to add or intensify alcohol service.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 41 approved in 2021 for 658 Vallejo (53 m away, North Beach NCD). Change of use to Restaurant approved April 2021 per amendments to §722 and §780.3 under legislation effective November 2020 that liberalized restaurant approvals.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning cited the 2020 legislation (Ordinance 182-20) that amended North Beach rules to facilitate restaurant approvals, showing the policy environment has shifted toward supporting existing eating places rather than restricting them.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 41 approved in March 2021 for 1318 Grant (85 m away, North Beach NCD). Approved under Ordinance 182-20 amending §722 and §780.3, which made restaurant use permitted at this location after the ordinance was adopted August 2020.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Recent approval under the 2020 Planning Code amendments that made restaurants permitted uses in North Beach NCD where previously they required CUA, demonstrating the shift from discretionary to ministerial review for established eating places.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 47 referral approved for existing restaurant at 1512 Stockton (105 m away, North Beach NCD) in 2019. Planning noted the site already held an existing Type 47 (license #343850) and approved continuation under §722 and §780.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Recent approval confirming that established restaurants with existing Type 47 licenses are permitted to continue under North Beach NCD and SUD rules, consistent with the treatment of Type 47 as a conditionally permitted use for bona fide eating places.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant continuation approved in 2018 for 431 Columbus (same block, 53 m away, North Beach NCD). Planning approved as continuation of existing restaurant use with no expansion, consistent with CUA approval under Case No. 2007.1256C.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral: Planning treated restaurant continuation on this block as permitted under §722 and §780.3 when the use was previously authorized by CUA and remains consistent with that approval, establishing the path for intensifications at sites with prior approvals.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved in 2015 for change of use from vacant retail to Limited Restaurant at 1318 Grant (85 m away, North Beach NCD). While not a license upgrade, shows Planning Commission approved new restaurant use in the dense North Beach corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Use decision: Planning Commission approved a new Limited Restaurant use in North Beach NCD via full CUA, showing the Commission grants approvals for eating places in this neighborhood when properly presented, even in high-density areas.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN) and business registration certificate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Every other city department requires the BAN before accepting an application. Register within 30 days of starting business; fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55–$700 plus $4 state fee). If the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk and publish it.

filing_playbook.action: File for the Health Permit to Operate with SF Department of Public Health, submitting the BAN, Location ID (LIN), and proof of a certified food safety manager on staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at least one month before opening. The $470 application fee includes the initial inspection; the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026–28 under the current fee schedule. Failed inspections push opening by 2–3 weeks, so walk the DPH checklist in advance.

timeline_cost.notes: This range is the time and government cost to obtain the Conditional Use Authorization, the ABC Type 47 transfer, and the Health Permit to Operate, when they are granted. The CUA typically takes 120–300 days from filing to final (including pre-application, hearing scheduling, the 30-day appeal period, and any continuances); the ABC Type 47 transfer adds 90–240 days after the CUA is final, depending on escrow, public notice, referral review, and whether a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required for the over-concentrated census tract; and the health permit takes 14–45 days after application when the space is inspection-ready. Government costs include the CUA filing fee (approximately $2,750–$3,150 in 2022, CPI-adjusted annually), the ABC Type 47 transfer application fee ($17,000 baseline, but the license itself costs $100,000–$450,000 to purchase on the open market in San Francisco, which is not a government fee but is the dominant cost), and the DPH permit-to-operate application ($470). These figures exclude the building permit (no construction stated), sign permit, business registration ($55–$700), seller's permit and EIN (free), RBS and food safety certifications ($110–$295 per person), and workers' compensation insurance premiums. The total calendar time from starting the CUA application to pouring the first legal drink under the Type 47 license is realistically 10–20 months. The day range is for approvals; a denial or withdrawal takes less time but has no predictable range because the records do not show when denied or withdrawn cases stop.

records_summary: 414 Columbus Ave sits in the North Beach NCD where restaurants serving alcohol on the first story require Conditional Use Authorization under both the base zoning district (§ 722) and the North Beach Special Use District (§ 780.3). The property has operated continuously as a restaurant since at least 1986, with an active ABC Type 41 license since 2016. The site history shows three Conditional Use approvals (1986, 1998, 2010) to upgrade from Type 41 to Type 47, add live entertainment, and add amplified music. The neighborhood is exceptionally dense: 60 food and drink businesses within 500 feet, 40 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 feet, and 97 within 1,000 feet. Despite high density, recent approvals nearby show the Planning Department routinely approves Type 41 and Type 47 upgrades for existing restaurants as continuations of use.
data_gaps: No conditions text extracted for the three prior CUAs at this address (1986, 1998, 2010), so cannot confirm closing hours, entertainment restrictions, or food-sales requirements imposed
ABC license conditions are not exposed in the dataset, so any existing operational restrictions on the Type 41 are unknown
The base rate excludes 102 grant-only permits and licenses, so approval patterns for entertainment permits and ABC transfers are not counted
No hearing transcripts or planner notes for comparable Type 47 upgrades nearby, so cannot assess what factors influenced approval
The density count uses a 500 ft radius proxy for undue concentration; actual ABC census tract data and crime reporting district not provided
No information on whether prior owners complied with the 51% food-sales reporting requirement under § 780.3(c)(2)(A)
